label: refusal re-audit — one recovery, three refusals confirmed against the engine catalogue

widget.prompt: Place D so that ABCD is a parallelogram, then prove it twice over: opposite sides with equal slopes, and opposite sides with equal lengths.
widget.successFeedback: D = (3, 5). AB and DC have the same slope AND the same length; so do BC and AD. That is the theorem: in a parallelogram, opposite sides are not merely parallel — they are equal. The slopes give the parallel, the distances give the equal, and neither follows from the picture alone.
widget.positionFeedback: The computed slopes or lengths still disagree. Move D until both pairs of opposite sides match on both counts.
widget.evidenceFeedback: It looks like a parallelogram, but looking is not proving. Compute the slopes and the side lengths before checking.

refusals.title: Opposite & Consecutive Angles
refusals.why: RE-AUDITED against the full manip>=2 catalogue, not one engine. The lesson is about quadrilateral ANGLE relationships — opposite angles equal, consecutive angles supplementary. coordinateProofLab proves parallelogram/rectangle/rhombus from slopes, midpoints and distances and never touches angles; triangleAngleLab sets one angle of a TRIANGLE; angleMeasure sets a single angle in isolation. No engine models the angle relationships of a quadrilateral. Refusal stands.

refusals.title: The Sphere Surrenders
refusals.why: Confirmed in S203L after the original reason ('no engine represents a sphere') was found to be false — volumeBuilder has solid: sphere. The honest reason stands: this step asks WHICH THREE earlier results justify the sphere formula, a synthesis question about the structure of a proof rather than a quantity anyone can build.

refusals.title: Reading a Study's Design
refusals.why: RE-AUDITED. 'The same finding, four designs — watch a claim shrink as the design weakens.' The nearest candidates model something else: samplingBiasLab's targetMethod is random|stratified, a sampling METHOD rather than a design-strength ladder; shuffleTest and sampleSim ask targetVerdict chance|real about one result. Nothing represents four designs ranked by inferential strength. Refusal stands.

refusals.title: The Statistics Detective
refusals.why: RE-AUDITED. Runs a five-question checklist over a claim. It is a synthesis of the whole course, and the thing being manipulated would have to be the reasoning itself. No engine models that, and a checklist lesson may legitimately BE a Tier C lesson. Refusal stands.
